transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's a pleasure to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. Well, I'm here because... honestly, I had an incident at work recently. 

I was on a board call, and someone asked a pretty small, routine question about the facility budget. And I just... I completely snapped at them. I lost my temper over basically nothing. That's just not how I run my company, and it is certainly not how I treat people. It shook me up a bit, so I figured I needed to come in and talk to someone to figure out what's going on with me.
Looking back over your life, would you say that you often feel indifferent to how your actions affect other people's feelings or well-being?

No, I... I wouldn't say that at all. Honestly, that's exactly why I'm sitting here today. If I didn't care about how I treated people, I wouldn't have been so bothered by snapping at that guy on the call. 

I've always tried to be fair and mindful of my team. You don't build a successful business by walking all over people and not giving a damn about the damage. So, no, I've never really been the type to just ignore how my actions affect folks. That's why this whole thing has me so thrown off.
Aside from this recent incident, have you been feeling persistently sad, empty, or down for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least the past two years?

No, not at all. I haven't been walking around sad or feeling empty... definitely not for two years. Up until recently, I've been feeling fine. I keep busy with the business, and my mood has always been pretty steady. It really is just this recent thing that has me feeling out of sorts.
Was there any specific, significant change or stressful event in your life or at your company that occurred in the weeks leading up to this incident?

Well, yes. About six days ago, we were doing a walkthrough of one of our facilities, and... there was an explosion. A fire broke out. It was a pretty major incident. So, yeah, this whole thing with my temper and feeling so off, it's been going on for about six days, right after that happened.
Since the explosion occurred, have you found yourself having unwanted, intrusive thoughts or vivid memories of the event popping into your mind when you are trying to focus on other things?

Yeah, I have. I'll just be in the middle of a work call, or, you know, sitting at my desk looking at the numbers, and... the blast and that fire over by the loading area just jump right back into my head. 

It happens out of nowhere. It's like a bad film I didn't ask to see, just playing right when I'm trying to focus on something else.

Aside from the intrusive thoughts, have you experienced any other symptoms related to the explosion, such as feeling detached from your body or having trouble remembering specific details about the event?

My memory of it is clear, I remember the details fine. But... yeah, that feeling detached part. I've actually noticed that a bit. 

Sometimes when I'm taking work calls from home, the room just looks kind of... distant. And my own voice sounds really strange to me. It's almost like I'm watching myself talk instead of being fully there in the room. It's a pretty strange feeling.
